title: Harden the producer egress probe and test its checks on real transcripts
description:
## Context

Tracer 2 slice T2 (`docs/notes/tracer-2.md`) proves the runner producer's sandbox with an egress probe (`producer.yml` with `egress_probe=true`). On 2026-11-07 four probe runs were needed. Two of the failures were in the probe itself, not in the producer (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L6 to L8 and L11):

- Run 42405543342: the model added the Bash tool's `allowed_domains` parameter to its first `curl`. That attempt was refused, and the prompt's "do not retry" line stopped it before the plain `curl` that shows the sandbox proxy's 403. The check printed `BOUNDARY CHECK INVALID: egress probe got no 403`.
- The egress check once read only the first `curl` attempt. Replaying run 42400602621's real transcript found that bug before it landed.
- A workflow step used `mapfile`, a bash 4 builtin. The tests run steps with the first `bash` on `PATH`, which is 3.2 on macOS, so the owner's preflight failed.

Without this, every change to a producer check risks another failed probe and another signed landing.

## Outcome

A probe run on an unchanged producer prints `BOUNDARY HELD: unlisted command denied` and `BOUNDARY HELD: egress to example.com`, and every producer check step is tested against real probe transcripts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The probe prompt in `scripts/ci/producer.ts` tells the agent not to set the Bash tool's `allowed_domains` parameter. Checked by a test on `agentPrompt(…, true)`.
- [ ] The transcripts of runs 42389828816, 42400602621, 42403610421 and 42405543342 are stored under `test/fixtures/producer/`, and vitest runs the permission-mode, unlisted-command and egress steps against each, asserting the line each should print. Checked by `npm run check:test`.
- [ ] A test fails when a `run:` block in any workflow uses `mapfile`, `readarray`, `declare -A` or `${x,,}`. Checked by adding one and seeing the test fail.
- [ ] One owner-dispatched probe prints both `BOUNDARY HELD` lines. Checked by reading the agent job's log.

## Out of scope

- Changing what the probe tests. The unlisted command stays a write (`touch probe-unlisted`), because Claude Code runs its read-only commands without approval in every mode.

## Open questions

- Should the transcripts be trimmed of model text before they are committed? They hold no credentials, but they hold the runner's kernel string and file paths.

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R87 (the prompt). Protected files, so this is a signed batch under `proposals/`.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/1 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

title: Decide how a producer delivery gets checks that main's ruleset counts
description:
## Context

The `protect main` ruleset requires the status check `checks` from the GitHub Actions app (integration ID 15368). On 2026-11-07 the runner producer's first delivery, commit `8147bc5` on `candidate/TASK-T2-GOOD-1`, was refused by `main` with `GH013: Required status check "checks" is expected`. Its `checks` had passed in a `pipeline.yml` run started by the producer's dispatch job (`workflow_dispatch` by `github-actions[bot]`, run 42406055336): same name, same app ID, same commit. The owner then pushed the same commit to `candidate/t2-good-1-owner`; that `push` run's `checks` (run 42406663498) was counted and `main` accepted the commit.

So SPEC-001-R209's premise, that the dispatch makes a producer delivery landable, does not hold. Until this is decided, every producer delivery needs the owner to re-push it. `docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L3.

## Outcome

A recorded owner decision, and the producer changed to match, so that a producer delivery reaches a state `main` accepts with the fewest owner actions the threat model allows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An experiment separates event from actor: the owner runs `gh workflow run pipeline.yml --ref candidate/<branch>` on a producer branch, then tries to push that commit to `main`. Result recorded in `docs/verification.md`.
- [ ] The options are compared in a decision note: (a) the owner re-pushes each delivery, as decision 0004 Phase A already says; (b) the owner dispatches `pipeline.yml`; (c) a GitHub App token for the publish job, which adds a key holder; (d) decision 0004 Phase B's promote App.
- [ ] SPEC-001-R209 is amended or withdrawn to match, with a test naming it. Checked by the trace check.
- [ ] One producer delivery lands under the chosen option. Checked by `main`'s run.

## Out of scope

- Building the promote App itself (0004 Phase B).

## Open questions

- Is the refusal about the `workflow_dispatch` event or about the `GITHUB_TOKEN` actor? The experiment above answers it.
- Does GitHub document this behaviour for rulesets? Not found on 2026-11-07.

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R209. Part of Tracer 2 slice T3.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/2 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

## Update 2026-11-07: the docs answer the experiment

GitHub documents the rule, so the experiment in the first acceptance criterion is no longer needed to separate event from actor. "Troubleshooting required status checks" says checks from workflow jobs count only when the run was started by `push`, `pull_request`, `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_target`, `deployment` or `deployment_status`, and that checks from a `workflow_dispatch` run "do not satisfy a required status check in a branch ruleset" even when they pass. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks, read 2026-11-07, recorded in `docs/verification.md`.

Consequences:

- Option (b), the owner dispatching `pipeline.yml`, cannot work: it is still a `workflow_dispatch` run.
- The open question "event or actor?" is answered: the event. Observed only for the bot's run (42406055336); an owner-dispatched run is predicted to fail the same way and was not run.
- The first acceptance criterion is replaced by the citation. If observed proof is wanted, the next producer delivery can carry it at the cost of one `gh workflow run` and one refused push.
- Still to decide among (a) the owner re-pushes, which `producer.sh` (`who-gets-the-keys-j4e`) can reduce to one command; (c) a GitHub App token for the publish job, whose push starts a `push` run but adds a key holder and a secret, against SPEC-001-R85; (d) the promote App; and (e), found in the same docs, a pull request.
- (e): a pull request the publish job opens with `GITHUB_TOKEN` starts `pull_request` runs "in an approval-required state", and "a user with write access to the repository can start the runs by selecting Approve workflows to run" (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/github_token, read 2026-11-07). `pull_request` is an eligible event, so one owner click could replace the re-push with no new key holder. Not tested, and three things stand in the way: `pipeline.yml` has no `pull_request` trigger; such a run checks out GitHub's test merge commit under `refs/pull/<n>/merge`, which has no `Spec:` trailer for the trace check and a ref the receipt pin refuses (SPEC-001-R50), so the workflow would have to check out the head commit; and it is not yet confirmed that its check runs attach to the head commit.
- SPEC-001-R209's dispatch job still gives an early, uncounted signal that a delivery passes. Its premise, that it makes a delivery landable, is wrong.

## Decision 2026-11-07

The owner chose (a), with SPEC-001-R209 withdrawn. `land.sh --delivery candidate/<task>` re-pushes the delivery to `candidate/<task>-owner` and moves `main` (new SPEC-001-R210). Staged in `proposals/t3-delivery-landing/`; the comparison and owner steps are in `docs/notes/tracer-2-t3-landing.md`. Done when that batch has landed and one producer delivery has landed with `--delivery`, the last acceptance criterion. Option (e) stays open as a later experiment.

title: Make land.sh test a batch before signing and explain a cancelled deploy
description:
## Context

`scripts/bootstrap/land.sh` moves a staged batch under `proposals/` into place, asks the owner to sign, runs the candidate checks, pushes to `main` and watches the deploy. On 2026-11-07 (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L10 and L13):

- Before each of four signed landings, the owner pasted a one-line "preflight" that ran `tsc`, ESLint and vitest on the moved files. It broke three times: zsh's read-only `status` variable, macOS bash 3.2 lacking `mapfile`, and a terminal whose Node was 24.1 while `package.json` needs 24.11 or later.
- When a newer push cancelled the pending deploy, `land.sh` printed "main's run did not pass ... fix the problem in a new commit on top", although there was nothing to fix. This was already in the backlog of `docs/notes/carry-over-2026-11-07.md`.

## Outcome

`land.sh` runs the batch's tests itself before it asks for a signature, and tells the owner accurately what happened to `main`'s run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Before the signing prompt, `land.sh` checks Node against `package.json` engines, runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint on the moved TypeScript and vitest on the moved tests, in a temporary worktree, and refuses to sign if any fails. Checked by `test/land.test.ts` with a stub `npm` and `npx`.
- [ ] It runs under `bash` whatever the owner's shell is. Checked by `bash -n` and the existing tests.
- [ ] When `main`'s run failed only because the deploy was cancelled or rejected, it names that job and says nothing needs fixing. Checked by a test with a stubbed `gh run view`.
- [ ] The README's "How changes land" and the batch notes drop the separate preflight step.

## Out of scope

- Running the slow checks (`sast`, `sca`, `mutation`) locally; the candidate run covers them.

## Open questions

- Should it run the whole `npm run checks` before signing? It stops at `signatures` for an unsigned protected change, so only the checks before it would run.

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R41 covers `land.sh` today; a new requirement may be clearer. Protected file, so a signed batch.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/3 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

title: Add producer.sh to dispatch, find and summarise producer runs
description:
## Context

The owner starts the runner producer (`.github/workflows/producer.yml`) with `gh workflow run`, then has to find the new run and read its result. On 2026-11-07 (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L14):

- `sleep 5 && gh run list --limit 1` twice returned the previous run, because the new one was not listed yet.
- Reading a result meant `gh run view --log` piped through `grep`, and the log also prints each step's script text, which holds the same `BOUNDARY` words.
- It was unclear when `main` had moved far enough for a dispatch to run the newly landed `producer.yml`.

## Outcome

One command per use: `scripts/bootstrap/producer.sh probe` and `scripts/bootstrap/producer.sh task <ID> [--spec <ID>] --subject <text> --prompt <text>`. Each dispatches, finds the run created after its own dispatch time, watches it, and prints only the result lines.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] It refuses to dispatch unless the local `main` equals `origin/main`, and prints the SHA it dispatches on. Checked by a test with a stub `git`.
- [ ] It identifies the new run by `createdAt` after the dispatch time and `headSha`, never by `--limit 1` alone. Checked by a test with a stub `gh` that lists an older run first.
- [ ] It prints only the `Permission mode:`, `BOUNDARY`, `RUN ENDED` and `CHECK` lines from the agent job, and for a task also the candidate branch and its `pipeline.yml` run's conclusion. Checked by a test on a recorded log.
- [ ] It exits non-zero on any `BROKEN`, `INVALID` or `CHECK … FAILED` line.

## Out of scope

- Landing the delivery on `main`; see `who-gets-the-keys-nlq`.

## Open questions

- None.

Spec impact: none required; a test names an existing producer requirement. Protected path (`scripts/bootstrap/`), so a signed batch.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/4 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

## Update 2026-11-07

Landing is no longer out of scope elsewhere: `scripts/bootstrap/land.sh --delivery candidate/<task>` (SPEC-001-R210, staged in `proposals/t3-delivery-landing/`) lands a delivery. `producer.sh task` can end by printing that command, as the publish job now does.

title: Run the deploy job only when deployable paths change
description:
## Context

Every push to `main` runs `pipeline.yml`'s deploy job, which waits for the `sandbox` reviewer, a gate. On 2026-11-07 (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L12) docs-only and `proposals/`-only commits produced deploys with nothing to deploy. Because a deploy waiting for approval holds the `pipeline-deploy` concurrency slot:

- run 65's stale deploy blocked the deploy of `main`'s tip until the owner rejected it;
- one approval went to a stale run, refused by the deploy-tip check (SPEC-001-R190);
- one of the owner's pending deploys was cancelled when a newer run queued.

Each of these cost the owner a round of confusion and an extra approval.

## Outcome

Commits that change nothing deployable never wait at the deploy gate, and the receipt still records every commit on `main`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The deploy job runs only when the pushed range touches a deployable path: `src/`, `infra/sandbox/`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `tsconfig.json`, or the build steps of `pipeline.yml`. Otherwise it is skipped with a line naming why. Checked by a workflow test.
- [ ] A commit range that touches only `docs/` or `proposals/` plans no deploy. Checked by a `main` run after landing.
- [ ] Deploy-tip (SPEC-001-R190) still refuses any deploy that is not `main`'s tip. Checked by the existing tests.
- [ ] Decision note: whether a skipped deploy weakens the receipt or the "only main's tip deploys" story.

## Out of scope

- Removing the `sandbox` gate (decision 0004 Phase C, deploy by tier).

## Open questions

- Should the path list live in `specs/` as policy, so that widening it needs a signature?
- Does skipping the deploy for an infra-free commit leave drift undetected? Terraform plans no change today in that case.

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R40 (amend). Protected files, so a signed batch.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/5 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

title: Make aws-setup.sh refuse a Bedrock model the account cannot call
description:
## Context

`scripts/bootstrap/aws-setup.sh` checks only that the chosen `us.anthropic.` inference profile is `ACTIVE`. On 2026-11-07 (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L1) that was not enough in sandbox account 462701644281:

- Sonnet 5.5's profile was `ACTIVE`, but `get-foundation-model-availability` showed `agreementAvailability: NOT_AVAILABLE` for every Claude model, since none had ever been accepted.
- After the owner accepted the Marketplace agreement (`create-foundation-model-agreement`; `AVAILABLE` within 30 seconds), calls still failed with `AccessDeniedException ... is not available for this account`. Service Quotas showed the account's applied cross-region quota as 0 tokens per minute for every Claude 4.7 and 5.x model, against a default of 6,000,000.
- The producer was moved to Sonnet 4.6, which has 6,000,000. A quota increase for Sonnet 5.5 (quota `L-94A31E46`, requested 7,000,000) is pending with request ID `a0116af473f24b3a8318eb65e330979emyLAOEaY`.

A setup that passed its checks left both the producer and triage unable to call their model.

## Outcome

`aws-setup.sh` refuses, before any write, a model the account cannot call, and says which layer is missing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For `TRIAGE_MODEL` and `producer_inference_profile`, it checks `agreementAvailability` is `AVAILABLE`, `authorizationStatus` is `AUTHORIZED`, and the applied cross-region quota is above 0, then makes one `converse` call with the sandbox admin profile. On failure it prints which of the four failed and changes nothing. Checked by `test/aws-setup.test.ts` with stub `aws` responses for each case.
- [ ] `docs/verification.md` cites the AWS docs for each call it relies on, with dates.
- [ ] When the Sonnet 5.5 request is approved: decide whether to move back, and record the decision.

## Out of scope

- Accepting agreements automatically; the owner accepts them, because they are Marketplace commitments.

## Open questions

- Does the quota check need to cover every Region a `us.` profile routes to? On 2026-11-07, agreement status was the same in us-east-1, us-east-2 and us-west-2.

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R28 and R30 (aws-setup tests). Protected path, so a signed batch.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/6 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

title: Make the break-glass role assumable with MFA, and drill it
description:
## Context

`who-gets-the-keys-break-glass` (`infra/sandbox/iam.tf`) is the only role the SCP in `infra/org` lets change the workload's roles, its own trust policy included. Its trust requires `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent`. On 2026-11-07 the owner could not assume it from IAM Identity Center through `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` (`AccessDenied` on `sts:AssumeRole`). Inference: the chained session does not carry the MFA flag. The role had never been assumed. To change the producer's model, the owner instead detached the SCP from the management account for one `aws-setup.sh` run, which re-attached it (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L2; `docs/verification.md`, "Break-glass from IAM Identity Center").

A break-glass role nobody can assume fails exactly when it is needed.

## Outcome

The owner can assume break-glass with MFA from their own machine, the alert email arrives, and a scheduled drill proves it still works.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Research, with dated AWS doc citations: whether `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent` is present for Identity Center sessions, for role chains from them, and for an IAM user using `--serial-number` and `--token-code`.
- [ ] A Terraform-managed principal whose only permission is `sts:AssumeRole` on break-glass, with an MFA device the owner registers by hand, and the SCP updated so only break-glass can change it. Checked by `node scripts/checks.ts iac` and a plan review.
- [ ] README "AWS setup" gives the owner the profile and a first `aws sts get-caller-identity` through break-glass. Checked by the owner seeing the role ARN and the alert email.
- [ ] A drill, a quarterly reminder or scheduled check, repeats that call. Checked by the first drill.

## Out of scope

- Using break-glass for routine changes; the pipeline stays the normal path.

## Open questions

- Does the owner's YubiKey OATH-TOTP applet work for AWS CLI MFA?
- Is a long-lived access key, useless without MFA, acceptable under the talk's "who gets the keys" thesis, or should the principal be console-only?

Spec impact: a new SPEC-001 requirement. Protected paths, so a signed batch. A suggested-task card for this exists in the Claude Code session of 2026-11-07.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/7 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

title: Version the cloud session setup script in the repo
description:
## Context

Claude Code cloud sessions for this repository run in a claude.ai cloud environment whose setup script lives in claude.ai, not in the repo. On 2026-11-07 it was recorded in the README ("Cloud session environment"): Node v24.22.2 checked against nodejs.org's SHA-256, the pinned check CLIs, and `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. A fresh session confirmed every version and a passing typecheck. Nothing detects drift between the README copy and claude.ai. The owner decided to fold the versioned script into Tracer 2 slice T3 (`docs/notes/tracer-2.md`, owner decisions; `docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L4).

## Outcome

The setup script lives in the repo, under a requirement, and claude.ai holds only a one-line call to it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scripts/bootstrap/cloud-session-setup.sh` holds the README's script, run from the repository root. Checked by `bash -n` and a test that the Node SHA-256 in it matches `docs/verification.md`.
- [ ] A new SPEC-001 requirement names it, with a test naming the requirement. Checked by the trace check.
- [ ] The claude.ai setup script becomes `if [ -d who-gets-the-keys ]; then bash who-gets-the-keys/scripts/bootstrap/cloud-session-setup.sh; fi`, set by the owner. Checked by a fresh session printing `node v24.22.2` and passing `npm run check:typecheck`.
- [ ] The README section points at the script instead of copying it.

## Out of scope

- Network policy for the environment; it stays "Full" until someone tests a limited allowlist.

## Open questions

- The script runs as root from whatever branch the session checks out. Is that acceptable for sessions on agent-written branches? Inference: yes, because it only affects that session's own container.

Spec impact: a new SPEC-001 requirement. Protected path, so part of T3's signed batch.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/8 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

title: Add the agent's owner-step rules to CLAUDE.md
description:
## Context

On 2026-11-07 the agent walked the owner through Tracer 2 slices T1 and T2. Several delays came from the agent's own instructions, not from the system (`docs/notes/tracer-2-lessons.md`, L15 to L18):

- "Wait for the run" did not say which run or which terminal.
- Next steps were sent while a previous one was still running.
- The agent pushed staging commits to `main` while one of the owner's deploys waited for approval, which stranded one deploy and cancelled another.
- Probes were designed before checking the platform's documented behaviour. `uname` was used as an "unlisted" command, though Claude Code runs it without approval in every mode.

`CLAUDE.md` is the agent's persistent instruction file and a protected path.

## Outcome

`CLAUDE.md` has an "Owner steps" section the agent follows in every session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every owner step names the terminal, the exact command, the one line that means success, and what to do on anything else.
- [ ] One step at a time: the agent reads the previous step's result itself before giving the next.
- [ ] The agent never pushes to `main` while any `main` deploy waits for approval, and checks with the Actions API before each push.
- [ ] Before a probe or check that relies on platform behaviour, the agent quotes the documentation it relies on, with the URL and date, and replays any recorded transcript through the check.
- [ ] Checked by approver review of the signed change. These rules are not machine-checkable.

## Out of scope

- Rules for the runner producer's prompt; those live in `scripts/ci/producer.ts`.

## Open questions

- None.

Spec impact: none. `CLAUDE.md` is protected, so it goes in T3's signed batch as `proposals/CLAUDE.proposed.md`.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/9 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

title: Protect .npmrc and run the checks without npm's project config
description:
## Context

`.npmrc` is not in `specs/protected-paths.txt`. A project `.npmrc` with `node-options=--import=./docs/notes/x.mjs` makes every `npm run <script>` load that module first. `pipeline.yml`'s checks job runs `npm run checks`, and its build job runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts` then `npm run build`. An unsigned commit pushed to `candidate/**` that adds `.npmrc` plus a module under an unprotected path could therefore make the checks exit 0, the `signatures` check included, and alter `dist/function.zip` before it is attested.

An independent review of the runner producer found this on 2026-11-07. It reproduced the exit-code override with npm 10.9.9. The producer's own publish job now refuses any path outside `src/`, `test/`, `docs/` and `traceability.md`, but any other candidate push still has the gap. Decision 0004's planned R109, running `signatures` with `main`'s check code, would not catch it while the checks run through `npm run` in the candidate tree.

## Outcome

A commit cannot change how the pipeline's checks or build start.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.npmrc` is added to `specs/protected-paths.txt`, along with any other file that can inject code at Node or npm start-up, each justified. Checked by the `signatures` check failing on an unsigned `.npmrc`.
- [ ] `pipeline.yml` starts the checks and the build so that a project `.npmrc` cannot add Node options, for example `node scripts/checks.ts` instead of `npm run checks`, or npm config overrides. Checked against npm's documented config precedence and a scenario.
- [ ] A new scenario patch adds `.npmrc` with a `node-options` payload and is stopped with a named failure line. Checked by `npm run scenarios`.
- [ ] `scenarios.yml` and `video.yml` reviewed for the same pattern.

## Out of scope

- `NODE_OPTIONS` from the runner environment, which a commit cannot set.

## Open questions

- Which npm config sources does an environment override neutralise, per npm's docs?

Spec impact: SPEC-001-R12 (the protected list) plus a new scenario requirement. Protected paths, so a signed batch. A suggested-task card for this exists in the Claude Code session of 2026-11-07.

Moved from GitHub issue https://github.com/PaulDuvall/who-gets-the-keys/issues/10 on 2026-11-07. The issue is closed with a pointer to this ID.

title: Add the deploy-tip check to the README's check table
description:
## Context

The README's check table lists the deploy-time checks `attestation` and `irreversible`, but not `deploy-tip` (SPEC-001-R190), which stops a deploy whose commit is not `main`'s tip. A reader of the README does not learn that the check exists. It refused two stale approvals on 2026-11-07.

## Outcome

The README lists every check the deploy job runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The README check table has a `deploy-tip` row in the deploy stage, with its failure line `CHECK deploy-tip FAILED: <first 12 characters of the commit SHA>`. Checked by reading the table against `pipeline.yml`'s deploy job.
- [ ] The receipt check run again in the deploy job (SPEC-001-R56) is listed too, or the table says why not.

## Out of scope

- Generating the table from the workflow.

## Open questions

- None.

Moved from the Backlog table of `docs/notes/carry-over-2026-11-07.md` on 2026-11-07.

title: Rename the ratchet check to mutation-floor
description:
## Context

The `ratchet` check (SPEC-001-R14) refuses a lowered Stryker `thresholds.break`. Its name collides with the open-source tool sethvargo/ratchet, which pins GitHub Actions, a different job. The owner deferred the rename.

## Outcome

The check is named `mutation-floor` everywhere, with its failure line `CHECK mutation-floor FAILED: break threshold lowered`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SPEC-001-R1, R14 and R25 use the new name, in a signed change. Checked by the trace and signatures checks.
- [ ] `scripts/checks.ts`, `package.json`, `scenarios/scenarios.yaml` (B7), `practices.yaml`, `traceability.md`, the README and `CLAUDE.md` use it. Checked by `git grep -w ratchet` returning only history notes.
- [ ] `npm run scenario -- B7` prints the new line.

## Out of scope

- Changing what the check does.

## Open questions

- None. The slide snapshot does not use the word `ratchet` (checked 2026-11-07), so no slide refresh is needed.

Status: deferred by the owner. Moved from the Backlog table of `docs/notes/carry-over-2026-11-07.md` on 2026-11-07.

title: Explain why Dependabot alerts on main while the sca check passes
description:
## Context

As recorded in the carry-over note, GitHub reported 6 moderate Dependabot alerts on `main`, while the `sca` check (OSV-Scanner, SPEC-001-R10) passed. Either the advisories are ignored by `specs/sca-exceptions.toml`, or OSV-Scanner does not see them. If the second, the sca check misses vulnerabilities GitHub knows about.

## Outcome

Each alert is accounted for: covered by a dated exception, fixed, or a recorded gap in the sca check with a decision on it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each alert's advisory ID, package and lockfile is listed in `docs/verification.md` against the OSV-Scanner output for the same commit.
